_about: Machine-checkable netlist for the handheld carrier board. The schematic is drawn in KiCad 10 at pcb/remote/remote.kicad_sch, and this file is diffed against it net by net. Prose version with reasoning: docs/PCB.md.
_check: Every connection below must exist in the schematic, and no net may have members that are not listed here. Extra connections are as much a bug as missing ones. This check has already caught a board-killing defect once: the XIAO was powered through its 5V pin with B+/B- absent, which silently removes battery charging.
_packages: Through-hole passives and module carrier. XIAO includes castellated SMD lands and rear battery solder-access holes. See pcb/remote/ASSEMBLY.md for assembly and fit limitations.

_schematic_refs._note: The schematic models the XIAO's pads as three connectors, because the module has no single symbol. U1.* below maps onto them.
_schematic_refs.J4: U1.D7 - U1.D10, U1.3V3, U1.GND, U1.5V (right row)
_schematic_refs.J6: U1.B+ and U1.B- underside battery solder-access lands.

U1.package: module, two 7-pin rows, 2.54mm pitch, 15.24mm row spacing
U1.note: Plain XIAO ESP32S3; external IPEX antenna. Rear battery pads require separate solder joints.

U2.package: round 14mm Robu module, 2x3, nominal 2.54mm pitch / 7.62mm row spacing
U2.note: CHIP UP, microphone port down over acoustic hole. Confirm physical pitch on 1:1 drawing.

U3.package: Adafruit product 3006, 7-pin 2.54mm row plus integrated 3.5mm speaker pair
U3.note: Footprint derived from official Adafruit Eagle board. J5 is part of this module.

SW1.note: Selected footprint; compare the owned button before fabrication.

SW2.note: 6A at28VDC silver contacts. Common2 VBAT_IN,throw1 VBAT_SW,throw3 unused.

J5.note: Solder module speaker holes to these pads with pins or lead stubs; do not install a separate connector here.

J6.note: Solder to XIAO underside battery pads. If XIAO is raised on headers, use short battery leads.

C4.note: U3 decoupling. Belongs on VBAT_SW, NOT on 3V3 - that error left the class-D amp with no HF decoupling.

C5.note: amp supply bulk - the one people skip

C6.note: ADC tap. NOT decoupling - load-bearing. See VBAT_SENSE.

C7.note: OPTIONAL button debounce. tau ~3ms against the internal pullup; harmless to ext0 wake.

R1.note: DO NOT FIT. Fit only in place of R5 to get 15dB instead of 12dB, after hearing it in the case. Never fit both.

R2.note: battery divider, high side. 1% because this is compared against a threshold.

R3.note: battery divider, low side. Must match R2's tolerance or the ratio is guesswork.

R4.note: OPTIONAL external button pullup. Insurance against the RTC-pullup wake-loop bug; costs 33uA only while the button is held.

R5.note: FITTED. Links AMP_GAIN to GND = 12dB, the build state. Remove to fit R1 for 15dB.

TP10.note: GND reference. Without one, none of the other test points can be scoped.

TP11.note: GND reference, opposite end of the board from TP10.

VBAT_SW.note: U1.B+ , NOT U1.5V. Powering the module through its 5V pin bypasses the onboard LiPo charger entirely - the cell never charges - and the LDO drops out as the cell falls toward 3.4V. U3.VIN on raw battery, NOT 3V3 and NOT 5V: the 5V pin is dead on battery; 3V3 costs ~2.3dB of output.

3V3.note: OUTPUT from the XIAO's onboard LDO. Do not drive it.

GND.note: U2.L/R to GND selects the left channel, which is what the firmware reads (I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_ONLY_LEFT). Floating = silence that looks like a dead mic. U3.GAIN is NO LONGER a direct member - it reaches GND through AMP_GAIN so the 15dB option stays available.

AMP_GAIN.note: R5 (0R) fitted = GAIN strapped to GND = 12dB. Remove R5 and fit R1 (100k) for 15dB. Never both - two paths to GND is just 12dB again.

I2S_AMP_DIN.note: GPIO3 is an ESP32-S3 strapping pin (JTAG source select). Proven working - DIN is a high-impedance input and does not hold the pin during boot.

BUTTON.note: INPUT_PULLUP, other side to GND. Must stay an RTC-capable pin (GPIO0-21) or deep-sleep ext0 wake breaks.

VBAT_SENSE.note: ADC1_CH5. Must be an ADC1 pin: ADC2 is unusable while the WiFi radio is on, which is always. R2/R3 divide by 2, so 4.2V reads 2.10V and 3.3V reads 1.65V - inside the 12dB attenuation range with headroom. 2.1uA at full charge, 3% of the 70uA sleeping current. Tapped off VBAT_SW rather than BAT+ so the divider draws nothing with SW2 off. C6 is load-bearing: the SAR ADC charges its sample cap from the source, and a 500k Thevenin cannot do that in time - without C6 the reading droops with sample rate and looks exactly like a failing battery. Its 50ms time constant also averages out the amp's switching bursts, so you read the cell and not the ripple on it. TP8 against TP9 verifies the divider with nothing but a multimeter: one must read half the other.

SPK+.note: J5 is the integrated speaker-pad pair of the Adafruit amplifier; routed to J2. Neither speaker terminal is ground.

SPK-.note: J5 is the integrated speaker-pad pair of the Adafruit amplifier; routed to J2. Neither speaker terminal is ground.

AMP_SD_SAFE.note: 2.2k limits SD injection; 10k pull-down keeps amp shut down with GPIO floating.

no_connect._note: Each of these carries its OWN no-connect flag. They must never share a net: D6 and D7 are UART0 TX and RX, and putting them on a common net - however it is labelled - shorts the serial console to itself. That defect was present in the first schematic.
no_connect.U1.D6: GPIO43 - UART0 TX, left clear so serial debugging keeps working
no_connect.U1.5V: only live on USB, useless on battery. NEVER power the module through it - see VBAT_SW.
no_connect.SW2.NC: unused throw of the isolation switch

firmware_pins._note: Must match firmware/remote/remote.ino. Change both together or nothing works and it looks like a hardware fault. Verified against the schematic on 2026-09-04: all 8 signal pins land on the correct connector pin. BATT_SENSE_PIN is the exception - the board reserves it, the firmware does not read it yet. That is Phase 4, and deliberately not a reason to delay the board.
firmware_pins._led_note: LED_PIN 21 is the module's onboard LED and is NOT brought out to the 14-pin header, so it cannot be mirrored to a panel LED - and no GPIO is free to drive one. Once the case is sealed, every blink code is invisible. A light pipe over the module is the only route.
